questions.question: A hotel brand that adds the phrase "Rest like you're home" to its ads after many guests wrote reviews saying it felt like home is
questions.explanation: Drawing on the customer voice. The customer voice is what customers say about a brand in reviews, surveys and social media. When a brand uses customers' own words in its messaging, its claims feel more authentic and believable. The hotel is clearly listening to feedback rather than ignoring it, nothing suggests it copied a competitor, and the slogan has nothing to do with prices. Brands that pay attention to the customer voice can also discover strengths they hadn't emphasized before.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the role of customer voice in branding

questions.question: Nia wants her team to try a new project-tracking app. Several teammates are skeptical. Which approach would be most persuasive?

options.A: Insist they use it starting tomorrow
options.C: Run a short trial and share the results
options.D: Tell them the manager will be upset

questions.explanation: Run a short trial and share the results. A short trial lets skeptical teammates experience the app's benefits for themselves, and sharing the results, such as fewer missed deadlines, provides evidence. Insisting on immediate use creates resistance, complaining about the old system doesn't show why the new one is better, and using the manager's displeasure as pressure is manipulative rather than persuasive. People are more likely to accept change when they see real benefits and feel their concerns have been heard. Involving skeptics in the trial can also turn them into supporters.

performanceIndicator.text: Persuade others

questions.question: When evaluating an online source for a marketing report, a student should check whether

options.D: the source agrees with her opinion.

questions.explanation: The author is qualified. Reliable sources come from qualified authors or respected organizations and support their claims with evidence, such as data or research. Bright colors and article length say nothing about accuracy, and choosing sources only because they agree with one's opinion leads to biased research. Students should also check when the information was published, since outdated data can mislead, and compare it with other reliable sources. Strong reports depend on information that readers can trust. A reliable source also explains where its facts came from.

performanceIndicator.text: Evaluate quality and source of information

questions.question: When coaching a new employee, a supervisor should give feedback that is
questions.explanation: Specific and encouraging. Effective coaching uses specific feedback, such as "Your greeting was friendly; next, try asking about the customer's needs," so the employee knows exactly what to keep doing and what to improve. Encouragement builds confidence. Vague comments leave employees guessing, only negative feedback discourages them, and feedback given only at yearly reviews comes too late to help with daily work. Good coaches also ask questions and let employees practice, so they learn by doing. Regular, short coaching conversations are often more effective than long, infrequent ones.

performanceIndicator.text: Coach others

questions.question: A small company wants to collect customers' email addresses and purchase history to send targeted promotions. Which legal issue should it consider first?
questions.explanation: Privacy laws. Collecting and using customers' personal information is governed by privacy and data protection laws, which may require businesses to explain how data is used, protect it and let customers opt out of marketing. Minimum wage laws concern employee pay, zoning laws govern land use, and vehicle registration laws apply to cars. Businesses that ignore privacy laws can face fines and lose customers' trust, so many create clear privacy policies before collecting data. Some states have stricter privacy rules than federal law, so businesses must check where their customers live.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe legal issues affecting businesses

questions.question: When a popular toy suddenly becomes much more expensive to produce and supply falls while demand stays the same, its price usually
questions.explanation: Rises. When supply decreases and demand stays the same, fewer products are available for the same number of buyers. Buyers compete for the limited supply, so prices rise. Prices would fall if supply increased or demand dropped, they rarely stay exactly the same when supply changes this much, and they wouldn't drop to zero for a popular product. Understanding supply and demand helps businesses predict price changes and decide how much to produce. Businesses that sell products with limited supply often raise prices for the same reason.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the principles of supply and demand

questions.question: A U.S. sneaker company designs its shoes in Oregon, manufactures them in Indonesia and sells them in 40 countries. This shows that the company operates in
questions.explanation: A global environment. In a global business environment, companies design, produce and sell products across many countries. This creates opportunities, such as access to new customers and lower production costs, but also challenges, such as currency changes, different laws and shipping delays. A purely local market serves one area, a command economy is controlled by the government, and a closed economy doesn't trade with other countries. Global companies must watch economic and political conditions in every country where they operate.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the global environment in which businesses operate

questions.question: Which of the following is a difference between a credit union and a commercial bank:

options.A: Banks are owned by the government
options.B: Credit unions are owned by members
options.C: Credit unions can't offer savings accounts

questions.explanation: Credit unions are owned by members. Credit unions are not-for-profit financial institutions owned by their members, who usually share a common bond, such as an employer or community. Commercial banks are businesses owned by shareholders and run to earn profits. Credit unions do offer savings accounts, most banks are privately owned rather than government-owned, and banks make loans as a core business. Because credit unions don't need to earn profits for shareholders, they may offer lower loan rates or fewer fees.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe types of financial-services providers

questions.question: A business that publishes false online claims that a competitor's products are dangerous may be sued for
questions.explanation: Defamation. Defamation is a tort, or civil wrong, involving false statements that damage someone's reputation, including a business's reputation. Written defamation is called libel. The competitor could sue for damages if the claims are false and hurt its sales. A breach of warranty involves failing to keep a promise about a product, trademark registration protects brand names, and price fixing is an illegal agreement among competitors on prices. Businesses can criticize competitors honestly, but statements must be true and supported.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify the basic torts relating to business enterprises

questions.question: Devin is coaching a new associate at a phone store who rarely suggests cases or screen protectors to buyers. Which approach would be most effective?

options.A: Model it, then let him practice
options.B: Take over all of his sales himself
options.C: Tell him to figure it out alone
options.D: Criticize him in front of customers

questions.explanation: Model it, then let him practice. Coaching works best when the coach demonstrates the skill, lets the learner practice and gives helpful feedback. Devin can model suggestion selling with a few customers, then watch the associate try it and offer tips. Taking over his sales prevents him from learning, leaving him to figure it out alone wastes her experience, and criticizing him in front of customers embarrasses him and makes him less confident. Coaching builds skills and confidence at the same time.

performanceIndicator.text: Coach others

questions.question: A furniture company that decides which stores will carry its new sofa line is performing the marketing function of
questions.explanation: Channel management. Channel management involves deciding how products will reach customers, including which stores, websites or distributors will sell them. Marketing-information management gathers data for decisions, pricing sets what customers pay, and product/service management develops and improves products. The marketing functions work together: research may show where target customers shop, which guides channel decisions, while pricing and promotion must fit the stores chosen. Coins and paper money together make up the physical currency people use every day, while most money today exists as bank balances. Both are part of the nation's money supply.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe marketing functions and related activities

questions.question: Kendra accidentally sees a coworker's salary on a printer tray. Later, another coworker asks her what that person earns. What is the most respectful response?

options.A: Tell the coworker the exact salary
options.B: Post the salary in the break room
options.D: Hint at the amount without saying it

questions.explanation: Decline to share the information. Kendra learned the information by accident, and the salary belongs to her coworker to share or keep private. Declining to share it respects that privacy and avoids creating tension. Telling the exact amount, posting it or hinting at it all reveal private information without permission. She might also quietly return the document to HR or the coworker so it doesn't stay where others can see it. Respecting privacy, even in small situations, builds trust among coworkers.

performanceIndicator.text: Respect the privacy of others

questions.question: If interest rates in the United States rise compared with rates in other countries, the U.S. dollar usually
questions.explanation: Strengthens. Higher interest rates attract investors from other countries who want better returns, so they buy dollars to invest in U.S. bonds and savings. That rising demand makes the dollar stronger compared with other currencies. A weaker dollar would result from lower demand, and the dollar won't stop being traded or become a commodity because of interest rate changes. Exchange rates are also affected by inflation, economic growth and political stability, and changes in them affect the prices of imports and exports.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the determinants of exchange rates and their effects on the domestic economy

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a marketing business activity:
questions.explanation: Advertising a new phone model. Marketing activities help products reach customers and include advertising, pricing, selling and distribution. Advertising a new phone model is a marketing activity. Mining copper is extraction, assembling phones is manufacturing, and designing circuit boards is part of production and engineering. All of these activities are needed for a product to succeed, but marketing is the part that connects the finished product to the people who will buy it. Marketing activities also include market research and pricing.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe types of business activities

questions.question: When trying to persuade coworkers to adopt a new process, an employee should focus on

options.A: how much he personally likes it.
options.D: why their current work is bad.

questions.explanation: How the change benefits them. Persuasion works best when people see how a change helps them, such as saving time or reducing errors. Explaining benefits from their point of view makes coworkers more open to the idea. Focusing on personal preference doesn't give others a reason to change, criticizing their current work makes them defensive, and pressuring them to agree quickly can cause resistance. Persuasive people also listen to concerns and adjust their proposals, which builds trust and support.

performanceIndicator.text: Persuade others

questions.question: When an employee realizes she can't finish a report by the promised deadline, she should

options.A: ask a coworker to secretly finish it.
options.B: rush and submit work full of errors.
options.D: say nothing and turn it in late.

questions.explanation: Tell her manager early. Managing commitments includes communicating early when a deadline is at risk. Telling her manager as soon as she knows, and suggesting a realistic new date or asking for help, lets the manager adjust plans. Saying nothing surprises the manager and damages trust, rushing produces poor work, and secretly passing the work to a coworker is dishonest and unfair. Employees who communicate early about problems are usually trusted more than those who miss deadlines without warning.

performanceIndicator.text: Manage commitments in a timely manner

questions.question: For a contract to be legally binding, both parties must

options.D: sign it in front of a judge.

questions.explanation: Exchange something of value. Consideration, meaning something of value exchanged by each party, such as money for a service, is one of the essential elements of a contract. The others include an offer and acceptance, legal capacity and a legal purpose. Contracts don't need to be signed before a judge, the parties don't need to be the same age as long as each has legal capacity, and they don't need to work for the same company. Many contracts don't even need to be written, though written contracts are easier to prove.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the nature of legally binding contracts

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a right that business owners have in a private enterprise system:

options.B: Owning other people's property without paying

questions.explanation: Choosing what products to sell. In a private enterprise system, owners have the right to decide what to produce, how to produce it and what prices to charge for their own products. They can't set competitors' prices, take others' property without paying, or ignore laws, which still protect consumers, workers and fair competition. These freedoms, combined with the right to keep profits, motivate people to start businesses. Private property, competition and freedom of choice are core features of private enterprise.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of private enterprise

questions.question: A business owner who wants help choosing investments for the company's retirement plan should contact
questions.explanation: An investment firm. Brokerage and investment firms help clients buy and sell stocks, bonds and funds, and many offer advice and management for retirement plans. Pawnshops give short-term loans using personal property as collateral, payday lenders offer small, short-term loans with high fees, and check-cashing stores cash checks for a fee. None of those manage investments. Choosing the right type of provider for each financial need helps businesses get better service and avoid unnecessary costs. Some banks also have investment divisions that offer these services.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe types of financial-services providers

questions.question: In a shared office, an employee shows respect for coworkers' privacy by

options.D: not reading others' messages or files.

questions.explanation: Not reading others' messages or files. Respecting privacy means not intruding on information others haven't chosen to share, such as their messages, files, personal news or health details. Reading someone's messages, spreading personal news, searching desks and asking about medical records all invade privacy and damage trust. Many companies have policies against accessing others' files without permission. Employees who respect privacy create a workplace where people feel safe and can focus on their work. Privacy matters in shared spaces too, such as not reading over someone's shoulder.

performanceIndicator.text: Respect the privacy of others

questions.question: A marketing coordinator who must present the results of four promotions would organize the information most clearly by
questions.explanation: Using a comparison table. Tables make comparisons easy, because readers can scan across rows and down columns to see how each promotion performed on measures such as cost, sales and new customers. Random order makes patterns hard to see, one long paragraph buries important details, and removing the numbers leaves readers without the evidence they need. Organizing information to fit its purpose, such as tables for comparisons, steps for instructions and headings for long reports, saves readers time and helps them make decisions.

performanceIndicator.text: Organize information

questions.question: A marketing agency agrees in an email to design a website for a bakery for $3,000, and the bakery replies, "We accept." The bakery then pays a $500 deposit, which the agency cashes. Two weeks later, the agency says no contract exists because nothing was signed on paper, and it now wants to charge $4,500 instead. Which of the following is most likely true:

options.B: No contract can ever exist without paper
options.C: Only the agency can enforce the deal
options.D: The bakery must pay double the price

questions.explanation: A contract may still exist. A contract can be formed through an offer and acceptance in emails, as long as the other elements, such as consideration, capacity and a legal purpose, are present. Many contracts don't require a paper signature, and electronic communications can show agreement. Paper isn't always required, nothing suggests the bakery owes double, and both parties, not just the agency, can enforce a valid contract. Businesses should still write clear agreements that list the work, price and deadlines to prevent disputes.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the nature of legally binding contracts

questions.question: A marketing team planned an outdoor product launch event, but forecasters now predict heavy rain that day. Which response best shows adaptability?

options.A: Hold the event outside as planned
options.B: Move the event indoors or offer a livestream
options.D: Blame the weather service for the problem

questions.explanation: Move the event indoors or offer a livestream. Adaptability means adjusting plans when circumstances change. Moving the event indoors or adding a livestream keeps the launch on schedule while protecting guests and equipment from the rain. Holding the event outside ignores the forecast, canceling the launch overreacts and may hurt sales plans, and blaming the weather service doesn't solve anything. Experienced event planners often prepare a backup plan in advance, so they can switch quickly when conditions change. Adaptable teams often turn a setback like this into a creative new idea, such as an online launch party.

performanceIndicator.text: Demonstrate adaptability

questions.question: A marketing team's goal is to add new customers at the lowest cost per customer. It increases its monthly online ad spending from $1,000 to $2,000 and gains 200 new customers. Raising spending again to $3,000 brings in only 50 more. Which of the following is the best conclusion for the team:

options.A: The ads have stopped working completely
options.B: Ad spending should always keep increasing

questions.explanation: Extra spending has diminishing returns. The second $1,000 brought 200 new customers, but the third brought only 50, so each extra dollar is producing less than before, which is diminishing returns. The team should consider whether more spending is worth it or whether the money would work better elsewhere. Spending shouldn't always increase, the ads are still working, just less efficiently, and online ads clearly do attract customers. Marketers often test spending levels to find the point where additional money stops paying off.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the impact of the law of diminishing returns

questions.question: A bakery buys insurance that will pay for lost income if a fire forces it to close temporarily. Which of the following is the main purpose of this coverage:

options.A: To guarantee the bakery a yearly profit
options.B: To protect it from a large loss
options.C: To pay for the bakery's advertising

questions.explanation: To protect it from a large loss. Insurance transfers the risk of a large, unexpected loss to an insurance company in exchange for a premium. Business interruption coverage replaces lost income while the bakery is closed after a covered event, helping it pay bills and employees until it reopens. Insurance doesn't guarantee profits, doesn't pay for advertising and can't prevent fires, although insurers often encourage safety measures. Without coverage, a temporary closure could force a small business to close permanently. Many lenders require businesses to carry certain insurance before approving loans.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the concept of insurance

questions.question: A company that grows cotton on its farms is involved in which type of business activity?
questions.explanation: Extraction. Extraction businesses take resources directly from nature, including farming, fishing, mining and forestry. Growing cotton fits this category. Marketing involves activities such as promotion and selling, manufacturing turns raw materials into finished products, such as turning cotton into shirts, and service businesses provide intangible products, such as banking or repairs. A product often moves through several types of businesses, from extraction to manufacturing to marketing, before it reaches the final customer. Each type of business depends on the others to get products to customers.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe types of business activities

questions.question: Zara is writing a report recommending a new social media strategy. Which order would organize her ideas most effectively?
questions.explanation: Recommendation, supporting evidence, next steps. Business readers usually want the main point first, so starting with the recommendation, then giving evidence and ending with next steps makes the report easy to follow and act on. Putting next steps first or mixing in unrelated facts confuses readers, random facts with a conclusion lack logical flow, and evidence without a recommendation leaves readers unsure what Zara wants them to do. Clear organization makes a report more persuasive, because readers can see how each piece of evidence supports the recommendation.

performanceIndicator.text: Organize information

questions.question: A city hosts a major music festival, and demand for hotel rooms rises sharply for that weekend while the number of rooms stays the same. Which of the following is the most likely result:

options.A: Hotel prices rise for the weekend
options.B: More hotels are built that weekend
options.D: Hotel prices fall for the weekend

questions.explanation: Hotel prices rise for the weekend. When demand rises and supply stays the same, more people compete for the same number of rooms, so prices rise. Hotels respond to this higher demand by raising rates for the festival weekend. Prices wouldn't fall when demand increases, new hotels can't be built in a weekend, and demand clearly increases rather than disappearing. After the festival ends and demand returns to normal, prices usually fall back to their usual levels. This is why booking early for big events usually saves money.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the principles of supply and demand

questions.question: Liam finds two sources on teen spending. Source A is a 2025 survey by a national research firm that explains its methods. Source B is an anonymous blog post from 2015 with no data. Which source should he use?

options.A: Source B, because blogs are always accurate
options.B: Source B, because it is older
options.C: Neither, because surveys are never useful
options.D: Source A, because it is recent and transparent

questions.explanation: Source A, because it is recent and transparent. Source A is current, comes from a known research firm and explains how its data was collected, which makes it more reliable. Source B is anonymous, offers no evidence and is more than ten years old, so its information may be outdated or inaccurate. Blogs aren't always accurate, older doesn't mean better, and well-designed surveys are very useful sources. Evaluating sources by author, date, evidence and methods helps writers build reports that managers can rely on.

performanceIndicator.text: Evaluate quality and source of information

questions.question: A store employee wrongly accuses a shopper of shoplifting and keeps her in a back room for an hour without evidence or a reason, refusing to let her leave. Which tort might the shopper claim?
questions.explanation: False imprisonment. False imprisonment occurs when someone is confined against his or her will without legal justification. Stores may briefly detain a suspected shoplifter in a reasonable way when they have good reason, but holding a shopper for an hour without evidence can go beyond what the law allows. Copyright infringement involves copying creative works, breach of contract involves broken agreements, and product liability involves harm from defective products. Retailers train employees on detention rules to avoid these claims.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify the basic torts relating to business enterprises

questions.question: A bicycle store offers customers a 12-month payment plan to help them buy higher-priced bikes. Which marketing function does this activity represent?
questions.explanation: Financing. The financing function of marketing helps customers pay for purchases and helps businesses fund marketing activities. A payment plan makes expensive bikes affordable to more customers, which can increase sales. Selling involves personal communication to help customers buy, promotion communicates information to persuade customers, and channel management deals with how products reach customers. Many retailers partner with banks or financing companies to offer payment plans. This is why central banks work hard to keep inflation low and stable, since high inflation weakens trust in money.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe marketing functions and related activities

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why stores accept U.S. paper money even though the paper itself is worth only a few cents:

options.A: It is printed by each store
options.B: It can be exchanged for silver at any bank
options.C: People trust it and the government backs it
options.D: It is made of real gold

questions.explanation: People trust it and the government backs it. Paper money has value because people trust that others will accept it and because the government declares it legal tender for debts. Money with value based on trust and government backing, rather than on a physical material, is called fiat money. U.S. paper money isn't made of gold, isn't printed by stores and can't be exchanged for silver at banks; that ended decades ago. As long as people trust the currency and inflation stays under control, it works well as a medium of exchange.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify types of currency (paper money, coins, banknotes, government bonds, treasury notes, etc.)

questions.question: When a nation's unemployment rate rises sharply, businesses that sell luxury goods usually see
questions.explanation: Lower sales. When unemployment rises, many households lose income, and others worry about losing their jobs, so they cut back on spending, especially on nonessential items like luxury goods. Luxury businesses usually see lower sales. Sales are unlikely to rise or stay the same, and no business is guaranteed growth in a downturn. Some businesses, such as discount stores, may do better as customers look for lower prices. Unemployment is closely watched by businesses because it signals how much consumers can spend.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the impact of a nation's unemployment rates

questions.question: A new marketing assistant who learns coworkers' names, offers help on busy days and thanks people for their support is
questions.explanation: Building good relationships. Positive working relationships grow from small, consistent actions: learning names, offering help and showing appreciation. These habits build trust and make teamwork easier, especially for someone new to a team. The assistant isn't avoiding responsibility, since helping others adds to his work rather than reducing it. Nothing suggests unfair competition or rule-breaking. Strong relationships also make it easier to ask for help, share ideas and resolve disagreements, which is why employers value people who get along well with others.

performanceIndicator.text: Foster positive working relationships

questions.question: A team leader who recognizes each member's contributions during meetings is most likely to
questions.explanation: Increase the team's motivation. Recognition shows team members that their work matters, which increases motivation and encourages them to keep performing well. Specific praise, such as thanking someone for a creative ad idea, is especially effective. Recognition usually raises productivity rather than reducing it, and when it is fair and shared across the team, it doesn't create unhealthy competition. It makes members feel valued, not ignored. Leaders who recognize contributions regularly often see higher morale and lower turnover.

performanceIndicator.text: Motivate team members

questions.question: Which of the following is a form of currency issued by the U.S. government:
questions.explanation: A five-dollar bill. Currency is the paper money and coins a government issues as legal tender, so a five-dollar bill is currency. A stock certificate shows ownership in a company, a store gift card can be used only at that store, and a credit card lets a person borrow money to make purchases, which must be repaid. None of those are currency. In the United States, the Federal Reserve issues paper money, while the U.S. Mint produces coins.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify types of currency (paper money, coins, banknotes, government bonds, treasury notes, etc.)

questions.question: A town's largest factory closes, and unemployment in the area rises from 4% to 12%. Which of the following effects on local businesses is most likely:

options.A: Local stores raise prices and sell more
options.C: Restaurants and shops see fewer customers

questions.explanation: Restaurants and shops see fewer customers. When many people in an area lose their jobs, they have less money to spend, so local restaurants, shops and other businesses usually see fewer customers. Some may cut hours or close. Stores can't raise prices and sell more when customers have less money, expensive vacations become less common, and demand for luxury cars usually falls. Communities hit by job losses often work to attract new employers, because unemployment affects the whole local economy, not just the people who lost jobs.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the impact of a nation's unemployment rates

questions.question: To protect his online accounts from identity thieves, a person should

options.A: throw old bank statements in the trash.
options.D: post your birth date on social media.

questions.explanation: Use unique, strong passwords. Using strong, unique passwords means that if one account is hacked, criminals can't use the same password to get into others. Sharing passwords, posting personal details such as birth dates and throwing away unshredded statements all give identity thieves information they can use to open accounts or steal money in someone's name. Other protections include turning on two-factor authentication, checking bank statements regularly and reviewing credit reports at least once a year. Password managers make it easier to keep track of many different passwords.

performanceIndicator.text: Protect against identity theft

questions.question: A snack brand notices that many customers on social media describe its chips as "too salty." How should the brand respond to this customer voice?

options.A: Ignore the comments because sales are steady
options.C: Consider reducing salt or offering a new version
options.D: Add more salt to stand out

questions.explanation: Consider reducing salt or offering a new version. The customer voice can reveal problems that hurt a brand over time, even when sales look steady. Testing a lower-salt version or adding a lightly salted option shows the brand is listening and may attract customers who currently avoid the chips. Deleting negative comments can anger customers and looks dishonest, ignoring feedback risks losing customers gradually, and adding more salt would make the complaint worse. Responding publicly to feedback also shows other customers that the brand cares.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the role of customer voice in branding

questions.question: An insurance policy's deductible is the amount the
questions.explanation: Policyholder pays first. A deductible is the portion of a covered loss that the policyholder must pay before the insurance company pays the rest. For example, with a $500 deductible and a $2,000 repair, the insurer pays $1,500. The amount paid every month is the premium, not the deductible, and agents earn commissions from the insurer. Choosing a higher deductible usually lowers the premium, but it means the policyholder pays more when a loss occurs. Deductibles discourage small claims, which keeps insurance costs down for everyone.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the concept of insurance

questions.question: For six weeks, Rowan's marketing team has worked late nights and weekends on a product launch campaign. Two members called in sick this week, and the others seem tired and discouraged in meetings. Which action by the team leader would best motivate them?

options.A: Ignore their mood and push harder
options.B: Celebrate progress and ease the load
options.D: Add more tasks to keep them busy

questions.explanation: Celebrate progress and ease the load. Motivated teams feel appreciated and supported. Celebrating progress reminds members of what they have accomplished, and adjusting the workload, such as moving deadlines or adding help, shows the leader cares about their well-being. Adding more tasks, criticizing them and pushing harder without listening are likely to lower morale and increase burnout. Effective leaders pay attention to how their teams feel, not just to what they produce. Asking the team what would help most also shows the leader values their input.

performanceIndicator.text: Motivate team members

questions.question: In a private enterprise system, the main reason businesses try to improve their products is to
questions.explanation: Attract customers and earn profits. Private enterprise allows individuals to own businesses and keep the profits they earn. Because customers are free to choose among competitors, businesses improve products to attract buyers and earn more profit. Government production quotas belong to command economies, businesses in private enterprise still pay taxes, and laws generally protect competition rather than reduce it. The profit motive encourages innovation, efficiency and better customer service, which benefits consumers. This system relies on consumers' freedom to choose which businesses to support. Competition also pushes businesses to keep prices reasonable.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of private enterprise

questions.question: A bakery adds a third baker to its small kitchen, but total output increases less than it did when the second baker was added. This illustrates
questions.explanation: Diminishing returns. The law of diminishing returns says that adding more of one input, such as workers, while other inputs, such as kitchen space and ovens, stay fixed eventually produces smaller increases in output. The third baker has less space and equipment to work with, so he adds less than the second baker did. The law of demand relates price and quantity demanded, economies of scale describe lower costs from larger operations, and the law of supply relates price and quantity supplied.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the impact of the law of diminishing returns

questions.question: A copywriter and a designer on the same team often disagree about ad layouts, and the tension is starting to affect their work. Which step would best improve their working relationship?

options.A: Agree on how to share feedback
options.B: Ask the manager to fire one of them
options.C: Complain about each other to the team

questions.explanation: Agree on how to share feedback. Talking directly and agreeing on how to give and receive feedback, such as discussing ideas privately and focusing on the work rather than personal criticism, helps colleagues work through disagreements. Refusing to speak makes the problem worse, asking for someone to be fired is an extreme response to a normal creative disagreement, and complaining to the team spreads tension. Creative teams often disagree, and those disagreements can lead to better work when people respect each other and communicate openly.

performanceIndicator.text: Foster positive working relationships

questions.question: A business that uses a popular song in its ad without permission from the songwriter may face a
questions.explanation: Copyright lawsuit. Songs are protected by copyright, which gives creators the right to control how their work is used. Using a song in an ad without a license can lead to a lawsuit and damages. A tax refund returns overpaid taxes, a zoning variance is permission to use land differently, and a safety inspection checks workplace hazards. Businesses avoid copyright problems by licensing music, using royalty-free music or creating original content, and by checking rights before ads run.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe legal issues affecting businesses

questions.question: While checking his free annual credit report, Tomas notices a credit card account with a $2,300 balance that he never opened. He hasn't lost his wallet, but last month he received a suspicious text asking for his Social Security number. Which of the following should he do first:

options.A: Ignore it because it isn't his account
options.C: Pay the balance to avoid trouble
options.D: Report the fraud to the card company

questions.explanation: Report the fraud to the card company. An unknown account on a credit report is a sign of identity theft. Tomas should contact the card company's fraud department right away, report the account and ask that it be closed. He can also place a fraud alert with the credit bureaus and file a report with the Federal Trade Commission. Ignoring it could let debt build in his name, paying the balance makes him responsible for charges he didn't make, and closing his checking account doesn't address the fraudulent card.

performanceIndicator.text: Protect against identity theft

questions.question: Which of the following habits best helps an employee manage commitments on time:

options.A: Starting every task the night before it's due
options.B: Relying on memory for all due dates
options.D: Tracking deadlines on a daily calendar

questions.explanation: Tracking deadlines on a daily calendar. Keeping a calendar or task list of deadlines and reviewing it daily helps employees plan ahead, spread out work and notice conflicts before they become problems. Agreeing to every request leads to overcommitment, relying on memory makes it easy to forget tasks, and waiting until the night before leaves no time to fix problems. Managing commitments well also means saying no politely, or negotiating deadlines, when one's schedule is already full. Breaking large tasks into smaller steps with their own dates also helps.

performanceIndicator.text: Manage commitments in a timely manner

questions.question: When the U.S. dollar weakens compared with the euro, which of the following is most likely to happen to American travelers visiting Europe:

options.A: European prices will drop by law
options.B: Their dollars will be worth more abroad
options.C: Their trips will cost more in dollars
options.D: Their trips will cost less in dollars

questions.explanation: Their trips will cost more in dollars. When the dollar weakens, each dollar buys fewer euros, so hotels, meals and other costs in Europe require more dollars than before. American travelers find their trips more expensive. Trips won't cost less, European prices don't drop by law because of exchange rates, and the dollars are worth less abroad, not more. A weak dollar has the opposite effect on European tourists visiting the United States, who find their trips cheaper, which can boost U.S. tourism.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the determinants of exchange rates and their effects on the domestic economy

questions.question: An employee who quickly learns a new marketing software program after her company switches systems is showing
questions.explanation: Adaptability. Adaptability means adjusting willingly and effectively when situations change, such as a new software system. The employee's quick learning helps her stay productive and supports her team during the change. Stubbornness would mean refusing to change, perfectionism means expecting flawless results, and dependence means relying on others for direction. Adaptable employees are especially valuable in marketing, where tools, platforms and customer trends change frequently. Companies that buy supplies abroad face the reverse problem when the dollar weakens.

performanceIndicator.text: Demonstrate adaptability

questions.question: A U.S. company that imports most of its products from one country learns that the U.S. government plans to place high tariffs on goods from that country. Which of the following is the most likely effect on the company:
questions.explanation: Its costs will rise. A tariff is a tax on imported goods, so higher tariffs raise the cost of products the company brings in from that country. It may need to raise prices, accept lower profits or find suppliers in other countries. Its costs won't fall, the products won't become tax-free, and competitors won't disappear, though competitors who buy from other countries may gain an advantage. Changes in trade policy are one of the biggest risks for businesses that depend on global supply chains.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the global environment in which businesses operate
